sources.title: Report of the OECD/NEA-Vattenfall T-Junction Benchmark exercise
A CFD benchmarking exercise based on flow mixing in a T-junction

sources.note: Experimental data are owned by Vattenfall R&D. Obtain and redistribute tabular datasets only under the applicable permission and attribution terms.

geometry.coordinate_system: Cartesian right-handed; main pipe axis +X; branch inlet axis +Z; origin at centreline intersection

junction_block.notes: Dimensions from Table A1 of NEA/CSNI/R(2011)5. The fluid-domain generator models the drilled fluid bores, not the external solid block.

geometry.fluid_domain_definition: Boolean union of the main-pipe and branch-pipe cylindrical bores; the solid test-block exterior is not part of the fluid domain

branch_inlet.measurement_plane_note: Distance is positive upstream along the +Z branch axis; the benchmark report uses its own signed coordinate convention.

main_19_c.method: linear interpolation of Table A2 between 15 and 20 C

branch_36_c.method: linear interpolation of Table A2 between 35 and 40 C

estimated_reynolds_numbers.method: Re_D = rho U_b D / mu using the tabulated water properties linearly interpolated to the inlet temperatures; these are derived estimates, not quoted benchmark Reynolds numbers.

inlet_profile_notes: The main-pipe inlet profile is fully developed and was measured at x=-3D_main.
The branch-pipe inlet profile is developing because the available upstream length is about 20 diameters.
The benchmark inlet velocity profiles were measured in an earlier test at main/branch flow-rate ratio 2; branch flow stayed at 6 L/s and the main flow was changed to 9 L/s for the benchmark.
The benchmark report requires careful inlet-profile definition; uniform velocity is a smoke-test simplification, not the benchmark boundary condition.
operating_conditions.property_reference: Use water properties from the 1967 ASME Steam Tables as specified by the benchmark report, with thermal-expansion data referenced to Incropera and DeWitt. Record the selected interpolation state and property values in every future physical-validation run.

reference_properties.source: NEA/CSNI/R(2011)5 Table A2 (1967 ASME Steam Tables; thermal expansion from Incropera and DeWitt)
reference_properties.note: Tabulated values are the report's guide values at listed temperatures. Future runs must document interpolation to 19 °C and 36 °C instead of silently substituting 20 °C and 35 °C.
reference_properties.interpolation_method: Linear interpolation between adjacent Table A2 temperatures for the values shown in fluid_properties_at_inlet_temperatures; future validation may use a higher-order property formulation if documented.

inlet_velocity_profiles.availability: described and plotted in report; tabular files were distributed to benchmark participants

downstream_piv.time_dependent_recording_note: The report describes 60 Hz time-dependent PIV sampled for 12 seconds in two separate sets; it also states 1424 image pairs in each of the 60 Hz and 4 Hz recordings at each measurement location.

reference_measurements.data_status: Reference locations and quantities are recorded; original Vattenfall tabular files are not bundled until redistribution permission and source files are confirmed.

downstream_ldv.source: Section 3.2.1 and Figure 2; upstream LDV planes are at -3D_main and -3.1D_branch.

uncertainty.piv_rms_velocity_note: Uncertainty is approximately twice the mean-velocity uncertainty due to error propagation.

comparisons: downstream PIV mean and RMS velocity
future_validation_plan.numerical_methods: Select and document turbulence/thermal model, temporal resolution, wall treatment and averaging duration before claiming benchmark validation.
future_validation_plan.smoke_test_warning: A two-step or otherwise short CFD smoke run verifies only runtime handoff and process completion. It cannot establish convergence, turbulence statistics, thermal mixing accuracy or agreement with experimental measurements.

future_cfd_domain.current_mesh_scope: Local T-junction test-section geometry only; main pipe end planes are at x=+/-1.220 m and the branch inlet is at z=+0.693 m.

branch.coordinate: z=+0.310 m in this OneFLOW coordinate convention

future_cfd_domain.future_boundary_requirement: The measured LDV inlet profiles are specified at the measurement planes, which are internal to the current local test-section geometry. A future physical-validation domain must be cropped or rebuilt so these measured planes become inlet boundaries; it must not silently apply those profiles at the current pipe-end caps.
future_cfd_domain.downstream_extent_requirement: The current test-section outlet plane at x=+1.220 m does not reach the furthest thermocouple station at x=20D_main=2.800 m. Extend the downstream pipe to include the 2D-20D temperature stations before attempting the complete thermal benchmark.
future_cfd_domain.omitted_full_rig: The full rig includes a greater-than-80D main upstream feed and an approximately-20D branch upstream feed. The current mesh does not model the full upstream supply system; the measured inlet profiles are the intended future boundary data.
future_cfd_domain.note: These are explicit future-domain requirements, not claims that the current smoke-test mesh is already a benchmark-ready CFD domain.

boundary_groups.note: The canonical OECD/NEA-Vattenfall Case meshes the original OpenCASCADE BooleanUnion volume directly and emits distinct main_inflow and branch_inflow Physical Groups. Its exported STL region manifest retains a compatibility inflow patch as the union of the two inlet subregions for generic STL-region consumers; this compatibility patch is not the Physical Group contract of the direct OCC MSH4 mesh.
